verdict: A handsome, well-tuned low-volatility origami slot that plays like Mystery Reels on a Buffalo board: its signature 'unfold' happens too fast to see and its free spins barely differ from the base game.
pros: Every measured band passes, and the low volatility matches the calm origami theme: 42.6% hit rate, dry-streak p95 of 11, 0.2% bust over 200 rounds.
Coherent, crafted flat-origami art. Every symbol is distinct at size, the animals read as premiums over the paper toys, and the folded tile corner carries the theme onto every cell.
Very readable wins: gold frames with the rest dimmed, plus a per-win breakdown chip ('Crane x3 · 2 ways = 3.93') that the player checked by hand and found correct.
Clear feature flow: the trigger bar ('12 free spins · 3 folded suns'), 'Free spin X of 12', a running 'Feature total' and a total-win card with the multiple of the bet.
cons: Make the unfold visible. Let the reels settle showing the blank Folded squares, hold for about 300 ms with the squares outlined, then flip them one reel at a time into the drawn symbol, and keep a small folded-corner marker on cells that were squares. Today the player never saw which tiles had been squares, and 'Squares → Koi' with no win was confusing.

Give Free folds a real difference from the base game. For example, make revealed squares sticky for the rest of the feature, or draw only premiums (Crane/Fox/Koi/Frog) in free spins instead of 68% lows. Then rebalance the strips so the feature carries 35–45% of the RTP with an average of about 30–40x, instead of 25.7% and 21x. Also change the intro line, since 'Folded squares open every spin' describes the base game too.

Add honest anticipation: when 2 suns are down and a later reel can still show one (every reel carries a sun), slow the remaining reels and glow the landed suns. Never slow when the trigger can no longer complete.

Make the special symbols easier to tell apart: put a short 'WILD' fold-label on the Gold foil diamond so it no longer reads as a second Paper star, and make the creased-paper landscape visible behind the board (lighten it a step or let it show through the frame) so the screen isn't just a navy box. Keep the per-win breakdown line in Turbo.
confusions: The 'Squares -> Koi / Water bomb / Paper star' label appeared on many spins, but by the time the reels settled I couldn't see which tiles had been folded squares, so I didn't know what the reveal had changed (often nothing won).
Before opening the paytable I wasn't sure the gold foil diamond was the wild; nothing on the board labels it.
In Turbo, multi-win spins only showed '2 wins = 7.07' without the per-symbol breakdown that normal speed gives.
